body:
THE CONTRACT IS `.adlc/specs/backlog-grooming.md`, committed on main. This ticket builds the READ half of §3: fetch (§3.1), classify verifiability (§3.2), verify (§3.3), cluster and relations (§3.4), relabel triggers (§3.4a), rank (§3.5), the report (§3.9) and the cache (§4). The WRITE half — the adversarial gate, the autonomy floor and execution — is ticket T-01M2DT4JCYDDTE818Y1MEGZZTK and DEPENDS on this one.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN LANE. This half writes NOTHING to GitHub. It cannot close a live issue, so it is safe to build and land independently, and it is useful on its own: it produces the groomed set. Keeping it separate means the write half's cross-model review stays focused on the code that decides to act, instead of being diluted across a body parser, a cache and a ranker. Nothing in the toolkit produced this split — `merge-forecast` measures inter-ticket merge pressure, not intra-ticket size (issue #1009) — so it is a human judgment, recorded here as one.

THE TWO THINGS MOST LIKELY TO GO WRONG, both already written into the spec — do not regress them:
- A mechanical check anchored to the cited LINE number closes live bugs. Any unrelated edit above the citation shifts every line below it, the snippet stops matching at that line, and a live issue verdicts `fixed`. The line is a HINT; `fixed` requires the snippet to be absent from the WHOLE file (AC13).
- The cache can reintroduce the decay this tool exists to detect. An issue with no referenced paths has no `contentHash` component, so a key degraded to `updatedAt` alone would never be invalidated by a code change and would return `valid` forever after the bug was fixed. Such issues are re-verified every run, or cached only as `unverifiable` — never as `valid` (AC16).

PRECEDENTS TO FOLLOW, not reinvent. All three are RAILS — read them, do not edit them:
- `scripts/release-audit-collect.mjs` `fetchIssues` — the §3.1 fetch pattern AND the truncation-honesty rule: a response of exactly the fetch limit is reported as `truncated`, never accepted as complete, because a capped list is indistinguishable from a complete one.
- `scripts/release-audit-collect.mjs` `ticketsByIssueNumber` — an existing index from ADLC tickets to the GitHub issue they backlink to. Reuse it; do not build a second.
- `packages/model-router/lib/floor.mjs` — not used by this half directly, but its fail-closed input handling is the model for §2.1 profile parsing: an unknown key is an operational error, never an ignored one.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC10, AC11, AC12, AC13, AC16, AC19, AC20, AC21, AC22, AC23 and AC26 from `.adlc/specs/backlog-grooming.md` §5. Each carries its own `verify:` command. Do not add or remove criteria.

OUT OF SCOPE: the gate, the floor and execution (ticket T-01M2DT4JCYDDTE818Y1MEGZZTK); `.claude/skills/backlog-groom/SKILL.md` (that lane owns it); filing new issues; modifying `issue-lanes` — its adoption of the emitted set is a follow-on ticket, which is why AC12 pins the schema against a committed fixture rather than a live consumer; reading issue comments as evidence.

edges.contract: packages/backlog-groom/lib/ — the verdict and proposed-action shapes the write path consumes
